title: An effective method for determining necking and fracture strains of sheet metals
author: Zhang, Shi, et al.
materials: Determine the location where fracture initiates, and the direction of the necking band. In the strain field immediately before fracture, the fracture initiation location is determined as the location where the thickness reduction or the major strain is the highest. Furthermore, the angle of the necking band, where the thickness reduction is localised, to one predefined specimen arm is determined.•

steps.title: Perform mechanical test with DIC
steps.instruction: Carry out the tensile test while acquiring full‑field strain data with digital image correlation (DIC). Prepare a random speckle pattern on the specimen surface, set up high‑speed cameras, and record images throughout deformation. Choose a frame rate that provides at least five frames between the localised‑necking time (tAN) and the fracture time (tF).

steps.title: Locate fracture initiation and band
steps.instruction: From the strain field just before fracture, identify the point of maximum thickness reduction or major strain as the fracture‑initiation location. Measure the angle of the necking band relative to a predefined specimen arm to define the band direction.

steps.title: Define BZ and RZ zones
steps.instruction: At the identified fracture‑initiation point, place two rectangular zones – the base zone (BZ) and the reference zone (RZ) – whose sides are parallel or normal to the necking‑band direction. Set the initial side lengths as follows (h = initial specimen thickness): WBZ = a·h with 2 ≤ a ≤ 2.5 (recommended a = 2); WRZ = b·WBZ with 2 ≤ b ≤ 2.5 (recommended b = 2); WL = c·h with 1.5 ≤ c ≤ 3 (recommended c = 2). For uniaxial tests where the necking band is at 45° to the tensile axis, orient WBZ and WRZ parallel to the tensile direction and WL normal to it.

steps.title: Fit strain curves and find onset times
steps.instruction: Using the DIC‑derived major and minor strains, compute the average thickness reduction in each zone (|ε3RZ| and |ε3BZ|) via volume conservation. Plot |ε3RZ| versus |ε3BZ| over the whole test. Fit two straight lines by least‑squares: one to data from 0 ≤ t ≤ tBN (where tBN = f·tF, 0.3 ≤ f ≤ 0.6; recommended f = 0.4) and another to data from tAN ≤ t ≤ tF (where tAN = g·tF, 0.99 ≤ g ≤ 0.998; recommended g = 0.99, or g ≈ 0.995 for equi‑biaxial tension). The first line should theoretically have slope k = 1. The intersection of the two lines gives the localised‑necking time tLN. Define the fracture time tF as the instant immediately before fracture.

steps.title: Calculate limit strains
steps.instruction: At tLN, take the average strains within BZ as the localised‑necking strain. At tF, take the average strains within BZ as the fracture strain.
